findings.reason: §3 states no replacement refusal for the archive route, and its own control (done-when (2)'s evidence that the sign test is *gone*) measures the opposite of a working guard, so the MAST source would silently accept a reversed flux family.
findings.text: §3 removes `PlasmaSlice.prescribe`'s fixed-orientation guard "in favour of the module's conformance refusal", but `translate_equilibrium` (nova/io/sourcemap.py:895) only refuses Data Dictionary reads; `PlasmaSource.from_mast` (nova/imas/plasma_source.py:146) feeds the same `prescribe` from the COCOS 3 MAST level-1 archive, and it is the archive path — not the DD path — that today's green test `tests/test_plasma_source.py::test_mast_flipped_psi_is_refused` (line 60) and `scripts/reconstructed_plasma_source/baseline_sign.py:49` (`raise AssertionError("flipped psi reached the current prescription")`) exist to protect, so a node following §3 deletes a live guard from a path §2's refusal never reaches

findings.reason: a node can pass §3's declared gate green while those three fail at the merged head, so the plan must name them (and the conforming pulse, 105052/1 or 105069/3, they re-point to) or the refusal's blast radius lands on the coordinator as an unattributed regression.
findings.text: done-when (1) requires `PlasmaSource.from_imas` to refuse DINA 105014/1, and done-when (3) scopes the gate to "the readers' test files … by delta against the base", but three currently-green, non-xfail `slow` tests drive `from_imas` on that exact pulse and belong to no reader's test file: `tests/test_plasma_source.py::test_dina_generic_source_reproduces_existing_prescription` (line 80), `tests/test_coupled_plant.py::test_dina_case_through_the_generic_source_is_unchanged` (line 843), and `tests/test_prescribed_plasma.py::test_polygon_flux_change_on_a_real_slice` (line 526, `from_imas` at line 548)

findings.reason: the census records both line numbers explicitly (row `extrapolate.py::Extrapolate.update`, line 37 of `docs/research/dd-cocos-census.html`), so the node's edit is the same whichever method the literal is attributed to; the misclassification only misdescribes it.
findings.text: §3 says "`nova/imas/extrapolate.py::Extrapolate.update`, whose `# COCOS` literals at lines 301 and 345 are reads, not writes", but `nova/imas/extrapolate.py:345` (`_levels = -levels[::-1]  # COCOS`) sits in `Extrapolate.plot_2d_masked` (defined at line 339, a plotting helper), and it negates contour levels for display rather than reading a COCOS-dependent quantity

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — `nova/imas/extrapolate.py::Extrapolate.update` resolves, but only one of the two `# COCOS` literals §3 attributes to it is in that method: line 345 is in `Extrapolate.plot_2d_masked`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the only negative control §3 declares is on `plasma_source.py`, so the requirement in done-when (1) that DINA 105014/1 be refused leaves three currently-green tests in files §3 never names red.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the only record §3 names is §1's durable census document `docs/research/dd-cocos-census.html`; its gate is the readers' own test files in-tree, not a scratchpad.
